_comment: Sponza + curtains test scene. Assets are NOT bundled in git -- run 'dev.py fetch-assets' to download the Intel Sponza glTF + curtains add-on into Assets/External/SceneBible/Sponza/{main,curtains}/. All paths below are project-root-relative, resolved by SceneLoader against the discovered project root regardless of launch directory. The camera + lighting setup is the classic Sponza shot: low cam looking through the atrium with a single directional sun slicing across.

camera._comment: Tuned via dev.py iterate-sponza loop against screenshots/reference.avif. 1 unit forward along corridor axis (horizontal yaw 11.3) from the original interactive pose, FOV 65 (vs 50 baseline). Local min of the RMS surface at iter17 (RMS 66.80) within a fwd / lateral / FOV sweep.

directionalLight._comment: Sun coming from BEYOND the atrium opening (-X bias so light travels -X), backlighting the corridor. Matches the reference's bright-back / dark-foreground gradient.

extensions._comment: Opaque per-module config. Each child key matches a registered scene-extension parser (see IRenderer::registerSceneExtensionParser).

render._comment: Per-scene render overrides applied at startup (SceneLoader.cpp -> Application.cpp). Each field has a sentinel meaning 'no override'; omit it to inherit RuntimeConfig / algorithm defaults.
render._comment2: remaining-tunable-coverage (B.80) sweep-check fixture: startup-config-coverage's render.normalMapStrength entry. sponza.json's own materialOverrides all set an explicit per-material normalMapStrength, which would mask the global field entirely (MaterialOverrideMatching.h: a per-material override always wins), so this fixture drops materialOverrides to let the global field reach every material.
